La recta de regresión de Y sobre X es la: The regression line of Y on X is the one that minimizes the sum of the squares of the vertical distances from the points to the line (least squares). It is used to estimate y knowing x:
Para estimar x conociendo y no se despej: To estimate x knowing y you do not solve that line for x; you use the line of X on Y, which minimizes the horizontal distances:
Las dos pasan por el centro de gravedad: Both pass through the centroid (x̄, ȳ) and the product of their slopes (the second written as dx/dy) is r<sup>2</sup>: if |r| = 1 they coincide and if r = 0 they are perpendicular. The coefficient of determination r<sup>2</sup> is the share of the variation in y explained by the line. An estimate is reliable if r<sup>2</sup> is high and the value lies within the range of the data; outside it, it is an extrapolation.

If each $y_i$ has its uncertainty $σ_i$, the line is fitted giving each point the weight $w_i = 1/σ_i^2$, that is, minimizing $χ^2 = ∑ ((y_i − a − b x_i)/σ_i)^2$. The errors of a and b then come from the uncertainties of the data, and the reduced $χ^2$ ($χ^2$ divided by $N − 2$) tells whether the line is compatible with them: close to 1, it is; if much larger, either the model is not a line or the uncertainties are underestimated.
